rulers.name: Leopold III
rulers.title: co-duke; Duke of Inner Austria from 1379

ledger.x: 1180: Frederick Barbarossa raises the March of Styria to a duchy.
1192: Ottokar IV dies and Styria passes to the Babenberg Duke of Austria, Leopold V, under the 1186 Georgenberg Pact.
1254: Styria passes to the Hungarian crown after the Babenberg line ends.
July 1260: Ottokar II of Bohemia wins Styria at Kressenbrunn.
November 1276: Ottokar II gives up Styria; the Habsburgs follow.
1379: the Treaty of Neuberg divides the Habsburg lands and Styria becomes the core of Inner Austria.
1456: the Counts of Celje die out and their Lower Styrian estates enlarge Styria.
1457: Styria and Austria are again in one hand.
1564: a second Inner Austrian Habsburg branch takes Styria.
1619: Ferdinand II, Archduke of Inner Austria, 'became sole rule of all Habsburg hereditary lands and Holy Roman Emperor in 1619'; the Inner Austrian line ends in the common Habsburg rule.
1804: 'Styria remained a part of the Habsburg monarchy and from 1804 belonged to the Austrian Empire.'
1867: in the Compromise 'the duchy was assigned as a crown land for the Cisleithanian part of Austria-Hungary'.
October 1918: Austria-Hungary dissolves and with it the crown land.

wars.name: Battle of Kressenbrunn
wars.outcome: Ottokar II defeated the Hungarians in July 1260 at Kressenbrunn; Bela IV ceded Styria back to Ottokar and the peace was sealed by a royal marriage; Richard of Cornwall recognised his claim.

wars.name: Austrian-Hungarian War (1477-1488)
